claims.text: Equiatomic CoCrFeNiAl has high configurational entropy relative to binary NiAl.
High configurational entropy in equiatomic CoCrFeNiAl induces significant local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions hinder atomic diffusion in CoCrFeNiAl nanoalloys.
Slower atomic diffusion reduces grain-boundary migration and grain growth during high-temperature annealing.
Slower atomic diffusion reduces elemental segregation during high-temperature annealing.
Binary NiAl has fewer local lattice distortions than equiatomic CoCrFeNiAl because it has lower configurational entropy.
Binary NiAl consequently has faster diffusion than equiatomic CoCrFeNiAl under the specified annealing conditions.
Binary NiAl consequently undergoes more pronounced microstructural coarsening than equiatomic CoCrFeNiAl.
After annealing at 800 degrees Celsius for up to 10 hours, CoCrFeNiAl nanoalloys will exhibit less grain growth than binary NiAl nanoalloys.
After the specified annealing, CoCrFeNiAl nanoalloys will exhibit less elemental segregation than binary NiAl nanoalloys.
CoCrFeNiAl nanoalloys will have lower measured diffusion coefficients than binary NiAl nanoalloys during the specified annealing.
Greater local lattice distortion will correlate with improved phase stability.
The comparison is intended to use approximately 50 nm particles with identical thermal histories and initial microstructural characteristics.
In-situ TEM can measure grain-size evolution during annealing.
EDS and APT can measure elemental distributions and segregation patterns in the compared nanoalloys.
Tracer diffusion experiments can quantify diffusion coefficients in the compared nanoalloys.
APT and diffusion measurements can directly assess local lattice distortions and diffusion behavior.
The prediction is bounded to annealing at 800 degrees Celsius for up to 10 hours in an inert atmosphere and to particles near 50 nm.
Changes in temperature, atmosphere, or particle size may introduce additional kinetic or thermodynamic factors.
Specific interatomic interactions may confound attribution of stability to configurational entropy-driven lattice distortion.
